newsitem.title: USA: Networks identify California death cult leader.
newsitem.headline: Networks identify California death cult leader.

text.p: Television networks on Thursday identified the man who led 39 members of the Heaven's Gate cult in a mass suicide in Southern California as Marshall Applewhite and showed videotape of him promising his followers they would rise to "a higher level."
CBS, NBC and ABC all identified Applewhite and aired a recent videotape showing him exhorting his listeners to follow the group's example.
"You can follow us but you cannot stay here," he said in one excerpt. "The planet Earth is about to be recycled. Your only chance to survive or evacuate is to leave with us."
CBS also aired videotape from 1974 in which Applewhite spoke of rising from the dead after he and his wife were questioned by police in Oregon when a campaign for recruits for his cult turned sour.

"And when we are (resurrected), after three and a half days, we're gonna walk out. Just get right up, and you're going to watch us," Applewhite told an interviewer then about his plan to find life after death in outer space.
CBS said Applewhite's body was among the 39 found dead at a mansion outside of San Diego.
In the recent tape, a shaven-headed Applewhite, who was known as "Doe" by his followers, delivers an infomercial-style lecture and urges people to "follow quickly."
It also depicts several followers, including one woman who is shown in an outdoor setting apparently discussing her decision to follow Applewhite's suggestion and end her life.
"Maybe they're crazy for all I know," she said. "But I don't have any choice but to go for it, because I've been on this planet for 31 years and there's nothing here for me.

"And they were saying to the person I was with that they felt the last, final ingredient would be for the vehicles to be dead, you know, what humans call 'dead.' And so I said 'Great. You know if that's what it takes, that's better than being around here with absolutely nothing to do.'

The tape originated from WTOL, a CBS station in Toledo, Ohio. A news assignment editor there said reporters obtained the tape from Rik Strawcutter, a minister in Adrian, Michigan, about whom the station had produced a story on a separate matter.
Along with the tapes sent to Strawcutter was a note labeled "to be issued to the news media."
"By the time you receive this, we'll be gone -- several dozen of us," the lengthy note said.

"We came from the Level Above Human in distant space and we have now exited the bodies that we were wearing for our earthly task, to return to the world from whence we came -- task completed. The distance space we refer to is what your literature would call the Kingdom of Heaven, or Kingdom of God."
The statement continues for several pages.
